description: A trigger sequencer of twelve rows, each row a line of hexadecimal digits where every digit is four steps

inputs.text: Each trigger here takes the sequence one step on
A trigger here puts every row back to its first step

outputs.text: A 10ms trigger whenever the step reached in that row is a one bit
The twelve rows as one polyphonic cable, a 10ms trigger on the channel of each row whose step is a one bit

notes: a row does nothing until digits are typed into its field and entered; the text is red while it is being edited and green once it counts
each digit is read as four steps from its four bits, so 8 is a step on the beat, 2 the usual hi-hat and 08 the usual snare
an asterisk in place of a digit is picked afresh at random every time it comes round
a row loops on its own length, four steps per digit, so rows of different lengths drift against each other
with the mouse over the module, the keys 1 to 9 put the cursor in that row's field
in a field, p fills it at random, r and l roll the bits right and left, and h spreads each digit over two; adding shift enters the result at once
feed the clock through a delay of a few samples so that a reset patched from the same clock lands first
menu: ShowLights — turns the row of lamps above each field on or off; the lit lamp is the digit being played
Random — opens a slider setting how many bits a random fill switches on, 0 to 100 per cent
Random length from — sets the fewest digits a random fill writes, 1 to 16
Random length to — sets the most digits a random fill writes, 1 to 16

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
